chunks: From him, with this chain, from Hashim and Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Hashim said: 'Do not be solitary (vaginal) and do not be female (anal).' Ibn Bukayr said: 'Do not be female,' meaning the females (anal) other than this place (vagina). The meaning in these two narrations is a type of dislike (karahah), because it is preferable to avoid it, even if it is not forbidden, which indicates that.

key_terms.الْأُنَاثَ: The females (referring to the female organ/anus in this context)
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: Dislike (a legal ruling less severe than prohibition)
key_terms.لَا تَفْرِدْ: Do not be solitary (referring to vaginal intercourse)
key_terms.لَا تُفْرِثُ: Do not be female (referring to anal intercourse)

ai.seo_question: Is anal intercourse forbidden or disliked in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies the juristic status of anal intercourse (al-Farth) by reconciling two reports from Imam al-Sadiq, establishing it as disliked (makruh) rather than strictly forbidden (haram). The term 'la tafri' is interpreted as avoiding the primary vaginal position in favor of variety, while 'la tufith' specifically targets anal intercourse. This reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that while permissible, it is preferable to avoid anal intercourse to maintain sexual propriety and avoid potential harm.
